verifier_note: All 13 citations resolve live - 8 DOIs via Crossref with exact title/author/year, 3 arXiv IDs via the arXiv API, the GitHub repo via the GitHub API, and the ICMPC10 paper as a full PDF on Goto's AIST site - so there are zero fabrications in this bucket. Claim-level numbers were checked against full text wherever obtainable (author PDFs for Chow, Henrich and Nakano; the arXiv preprint for NHSS; the PLOS manuscript XML; the arXiv PDFs for both SVS papers) and they are unusually accurate, including the 16-value NHSS duration table and every Cantonese statistic to the decimal. Two systemic notes: the one fully paywalled item (Sundberg 2007) has no open copy anywhere, so its '552 tones' and '+/-10 ms' internals stayed unverified while its qualitative core checked out on the abstract; and two findings (2 and 6) rest on speech data - the claim text labels this honestly in both cases, but their design implications generalise to singing without a bridging citation.

verdicts.verify_note: PMID 16564674 abstract verbatim: accompanists most commonly synced to singers' vowel onsets; lead/lag expressive, smallest fast tempo, longest slow. '552 tones' and +/-10 ms agreement NOT retrievable (Unpaywall is_oa=false).

PMID 27522944 abstract verbatim on both negatives: CVC context effect disappears once the number of legal choices is equated (benefit was response probability), and singers show no perceptual advantage. No numeric claims made.

PMID 27068550 abstract verbatim: N=149 listeners, 1/4/8/16/27 SATB voices; coda consonants are the principal locus; plosives /b/,/d/,/g/,/p/ confused; coda liquids /l/,/r/ too; density FACILITATES coda nasal /m/.

arXiv PDF Table 1 evaluates SEVEN vocoders (FastDiff, HiFi-GAN V1, PWG, NSF, DDSP-Add, DWTS, SawSing), not six; the MOS test used only 4 selected models + GT. All else exact; FAD 3.50/10.5 is HiFi-GAN in scenario (b).

corrections.claim: Seven vocoders were trained and objectively evaluated (FastDiff, HiFi-GAN V1, PWG, NSF, DDSP-Add, DWTS, SawSing), not six; the MOS listening test rated only 4 selected models plus ground truth, scored by 23 listeners (female singer) and 18 (male). Every other figure verified verbatim: with 3 h data every vocoder including HiFi-GAN mostly reaches MOS 2-3 only; in scenario (b) [3 min data, 3 h training] HiFi-GAN is 'only around 1, i.e., its generation is barely audible' with FAD 3.50 female / 10.5 male, while DDSP-Add and SawSing stay above MOS 2 and SawSing's FAD is below 1.0; the buzzing-on-breathy-sounds-and-/s/-/t/ quote, the 'cannot be reflected in any training loss function' quote, and the Parselmouth V/NV zeroing fix are all as stated.

verdicts.verify_note: arXiv PDF Table 2 names the baseline explicitly (Period Singer = 0) and has only two ablations: -Normalizing Flow -0.21, -Note boundary for MAS -1.13, so 'largest term' holds. MOS/CIs, 20 AMT + 19 Korean raters, 20 samples all exact.

arXiv abstract carries every quoted phrase verbatim: 33 systems evaluated, top systems' identity comparable to ground truth, residual difficulty is dynamics in breathy/glissando/vibrato, chroma-align + speaker embeddings best-correlated.

Author PDF: 23 speakers (13M/10F, mean 19.1); C-onset -15.77 ms SD 37.10 t(22)=-2.038 p=0.054 n.s.; V-onset +74.62 SD 36.75 t(22)=9.738; manner F(6,136)=11.439; short/long split and cross-language contrast verbatim. Measured on SPEECH.

arXiv:2012.00337 (preprint of the Speech Comm paper): all 16 Table-10 durations exact; MFA word-boundary deviation 25.30 speech / 103.90 singing, inter-annotator 5.70 / 8.70; 10 singers 5M/5F, 100 songs, 7 h. Sung population.

Quote verbatim in variance-temp-solution README; AP/SP confirmed as word-initiating alongside vowels. GitHub API: MakeDiffSinger BSD-3-Clause, openvpi/DiffSinger Apache-2.0 (upstream MoonInTheRiver is MIT). Repo created 2023.

ICMPC10 PDF: 29 entries (27 RWC songs/16 pro singers + 2 AIST-HDB amateurs), 15M/14F, 128 min, 1488 events, 438.5 s = 5.7%, 50-1225 ms, means 174.0-487.4, SDs 47.7-222.2, 1.6/1.7 kHz, 850 Hz-1 kHz, 97.5/77.7%. Invariance = Discussion pt 1.

PMID 7759655: exps 1, 2, 4, 5 as stated, but the claim omits exp 3 (only the practice effect was significant) and the authors' own outcome framing is RECALL of sentences; exp 5 'aid recall'. Synthetic SPEECH, not singing.

corrections.claim: Five experiments. Exp 1: subjects transcribed synthesized sentences better when preceded by a naturally produced breath intake. Exp 2: replacing the breath with the spectrally similar sound of rustling leaves had no effect on accuracy. Exp 3 (breaths before randomly selected sentences): only the practice effect was significant, with a non-significant tendency for breath sentences to be remembered better - this null result is omitted from the finding as written. Exp 4: appropriateness of breath size to sentence length had no effect, perhaps because the range of sentence durations was too small. Exp 5 replicated exp 1 using leaf sounds rather than silence as the control. The authors frame the overall result as improved RECALL of the sentences, so the design implication's 'costs measurable intelligibility' overstates what the paper concludes. Stimuli were synthetic SPEECH throughout.

verdicts.verify_note: PLOS full text: method is respiratory INDUCTANCE plethysmography (Inductotrace bands) + pneumotachograph, not optoelectronic (that word occurs only in ref 62). All else exact: 7 singers / 4 untrained, both F(1,9) values, PCA >98%.

corrections.claim: Respiratory inductance plethysmography (Inductotrace bands on rib cage and abdomen) plus a pneumotachograph - NOT optoelectronic plethysmography - measured 7 professional classical singers (2 M aged 39-41; 5 F aged 24-72) and 4 untrained males (21-41) during quiet breathing, the standard song Waltzing Matilda, and a free-choice piece. Everything else verified: both groups shortened time of inspiration and raised peak airflow when singing versus quiet breathing; classical singers used a greater percentage abdominal (equivalently smaller rib-cage) contribution to lung volume, F(1,9)>28.87, p<0.001, and greater rib-cage/abdomen asynchrony with the abdominal peak before the rib-cage peak, F(1,9)>28.92, p<0.001; PCA waveforms accounting for more than 98% of the variability showed consistent pre-phonatory inward movement of the abdominal wall in singers, absent in the untrained controls.

verdicts.verify_note: Author copy of the JASA paper: 22 classically trained singers, four vowels over normal range; every tuning strategy verbatim (sopranos R1:f0 all vowels + R2:2f0 often simultaneous; altos R1:2f0 low; tenors/baritones R1:2f0 and R1:3f0).
